question.text: Under SEBI's framework governing valuation for Category I and II AIFs, which of the following correctly describes the independent valuation regime?

answer.text: An independent valuer (eligible and independent of the manager, sponsor and trustee) must value investments at least once every six months, extendable to once a year with the approval of at least 75% of investors by value of their investment in the AIF
Independent valuation is required only at the time of investor exit and not on an ongoing basis
The investment manager itself can act as the independent valuer if it has internal valuation expertise
Independent valuation is mandatory only for Category III AIFs and not for Category I and II AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI framework for Category I and II AIFs requires investments to be valued by an independent valuer at a prescribed minimum frequency. The default expectation is once every six months, with an option to extend to once a year subject to the approval of investors holding at least 75% by value of their investment in the AIF. The valuer must be independent of the manager, sponsor and trustee and meet eligibility criteria set out in the regulations, and any material deviation between the valuation and a transaction price is subject to disclosure obligations. The Trap: Limiting independent valuation to investor exit ignores the periodic valuation regime applicable across the fund's life. Allowing the manager itself to value its own portfolio defeats the very purpose of the independence requirement. Restricting independent valuation to Category III only is incorrect because the periodic independent valuation framework applies to Category I and II AIFs as well. Note: The cited workbook chapter discusses valuation frequency, the investor-approved extension to one year, independent valuer eligibility, and disclosure and deviation obligations. The framing above reflects the general SEBI AIF valuation framework rather than a mandatory valuer-rotation rule, which is not specified by SEBI for Category I/II AIFs.
